methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates orthotopic/intrasplenic mouse models, scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, proteomics, multi-omics, and three patient cohorts, producing a multi-layered mechanistic chain (KIAA1199→GRN-EVs→hepatocyte PPARγ↓→SAA2↑→FPR2/EGR1 neutrophil→VEGFA angiogenesis) with converging genetic (OE/KD) and pharmacologic (rosiglitazone, WRW4, wortmannin, anti-VEGFA) perturbations and blinded MRI reads. Limitations include exclusive use of female mice (sex-generalizability untested despite being design choice), small animal group sizes (n=3–5 per in vivo arm; n=10 for survival), small spatial transcriptomic/mIHC validation (n=2 patients), and a prospective validation cohort of only 5 patients. Statistically, Benjamini–Hochberg is applied to omics but no multiplicity correction is described for the many pairwise Student's t-tests across dozens of panels, no a priori power/sample-size justification is given, missing-data handling is unspecified, and the KIAA1199–SAA2 nomogram is reported without clear internal bootstrapping or formal external calibration metrics beyond ROC. Effect sizes/CIs are not consistently reported; many claims rest on p<0.05 thresholds alone.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is predominantly preclinical (murine orthotopic/intrasplenic models, cell lines, EVs, scRNA-seq) with supportive human tissue/serum analyses, placing it at Oxford LoE 5 per rubric. Clinical relevance is meaningful but not practice-changing: the KIAA1199–SAA2 serum signature with nomogram addresses a real unmet need (CRLM risk stratification) and the identification of PPARγ activation and FPR2 blockade as mechanistically grounded interventions offers a plausible translational path, though endpoints are surrogate (metastasis burden, metastasis-free survival) and the prospective validation cohort is only n=5. Rosiglitazone has known cardiovascular safety issues (acknowledged by authors), tempering immediate repurposing feasibility.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE is most applicable given the predominance of animal experimentation, with supporting elements that would also invoke STROBE (observational serum cohorts) and REMARK (biomarker signature). The manuscript reports ethics approvals, humane endpoints, housing conditions, sex (female only), randomization/blinding is partially described (blinded radiologists for MRI) but not consistently stated for other outcome measurements, allocation concealment is not detailed, and no sample-size justification is provided. Data availability text references external GSE225857 and a Nature Reporting Summary but does not state deposition of this study's own scRNA-seq, proteomics, or spatial data accessions in the main text; materials are 'available upon reasonable request,' which is a weak reproducibility posture.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper proposes a specific and well-integrated axis—KIAA1199→GRN-EVs→hepatocyte PPARγ repression→SAA2→FPR2/EGR1 neutrophil—that extends prior hepatocyte-SAA PMN work (Lee et al. Nature 2019, cited as ref 40) and prior KIAA1199/neutrophil observations (Wang et al. Hepatology 2022, ref 22 from the same group). Novelty lies in (i) defining a transcription-factor-defined Egr1+ pro-angiogenic neutrophil subset arising in situ rather than from circulation, (ii) connecting it to hepatocyte PPARγ metabolic reprogramming, and (iii) proposing a dual-biomarker clinical signature. The conceptual framework is incremental over the referenced Nature 2019 hepatocyte-SAA axis but adds mechanistic specificity (PPARγ, GRN-EVs, EGR1-master-regulator analogy to FOXP3), warranting a solid novelty score without rising to field-defining.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly structured with a logical Introduction→Methods→Results→Discussion flow, informative subsection headers that map onto the mechanistic cascade, and detailed figure legends that are mostly standalone-interpretable. The abstract accurately previews findings. Minor issues include some typographical errors ('agonistt', 'intertumoral' vs 'intratumoral', 'might through FPR2'), occasional redundancy between Results and Discussion when restating the axis, and dense figure panels packing many sub-experiments. Overall writing is of near publication quality.

key_strengths: Integrated multi-modal evidence (scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, proteomics, EV biology, in vivo genetic/pharmacologic perturbation) converging on a coherent KIAA1199–GRN–PPARγ–SAA2–FPR2–EGR1 axis
Mechanistic chain validated at multiple nodes with orthogonal pharmacologic tools (WRW4, rosiglitazone, wortmannin, anti-VEGFA) and genetic manipulation
Identification of an in-situ-reprogrammed Egr1+ pro-angiogenic neutrophil subset is conceptually novel and connects hepatocyte metabolism to innate immunity
Translational dimension: KIAA1199–SAA2 serum signature with nomogram developed and tested across three patient cohorts, with blinded radiologist MRI reads
key_concerns: Only female mice used; sex-generalizability untested and acknowledged but limits translational scope
Small sample sizes for key validations (spatial transcriptomics n=2 patients; prospective cohort n=5; in vivo n=3–5/arm; survival n=10) with no a priori power calculation

Statistical reporting leans heavily on pairwise Student's t-tests across dozens of panels without multiplicity correction outside omics, and lacks effect sizes/CIs; nomogram validation lacks reported calibration/bootstrap internal validation metrics

Data/code availability is weak—materials and raw data largely 'available upon reasonable request'; no explicit deposition accessions for this study's scRNA-seq/proteomics/spatial data in the main text
Conceptual overlap with prior hepatocyte-SAA pre-metastatic niche work (Lee et al. 2019) and the group's own KIAA1199/neutrophil paper (Wang et al. 2022); novelty is substantial but incremental
Rosiglitazone translational claim is tempered by known cardiovascular safety restrictions (acknowledged); clinical applicability requires alternative PPARγ-targeting strategies
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a mechanistically rich, well-integrated preclinical study with a translational biomarker component appropriate for a strong Tier 2 journal (e.g., Nature Communications-level), where minor revisions addressing statistical rigor (multiplicity, CIs, calibration), explicit data deposition, and expanded prospective validation would strengthen acceptance; it falls short of Tier 1 due to incremental novelty over prior hepatocyte-SAA PMN work and limited clinical validation sample sizes.
